facts.statement: The only known fossil of Torotix is a partial upper arm bone found in the Lance Formation of Wyoming.
facts.quote: T. clemensi is represented by a single fossil specimen, a partial humerus (upper arm bone) recovered from the Lance formation of Wyoming.

facts.statement: Torotix lived at the very end of the Cretaceous period, approximately 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Its deposits are dated to the very end of the Cretaceous period, 66 million years ago.

facts.statement: Torotix lived along the shores of the Western Interior Seaway, though it remains unclear if it was a seabird or a freshwater bird.
facts.quote: They lived along the shores of the Western Interior Seaway, but it is not clear whether they were seabirds or freshwater birds

facts.statement: The fossil of Torotix clemensi was found in the Lance Formation of Wyoming, USA, in deposits dating to the end of the Cretaceous period, 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: El fósil de T. clemensi fue encontrado en la Formación Lance de Wyoming, EE. UU. en depósitos que datan del final del período Cretácico, hace 66 millones de años.

facts.statement: Later researchers suggested that Torotix was more likely related to the Charadriiformes, which includes waders and shorebirds.
facts.quote: Later researchers thought it was more likely to have been related to the Charadriiformes (waders/shorebirds).

facts.statement: More recent comparative studies have found Torotix to be most similar to the order Pelecaniformes.
facts.quote: More recent comparative studies have found it to be most similar to Pelecaniformes.

facts.statement: Recent comparative studies have found that Torotix was more similar to the Pelecaniformes.
facts.quote: Estudios más recientes comparativos han encontrado que era más similar a los Pelecaniformes.

facts.statement: The family Torotigidae was initially established to unite Torotix with the genera Parascaniornis and Gallornis.
facts.quote: La familia Torotigidae fue establecida inicialmente para reunir a este género con Parascaniornis y Gallornis.

facts.statement: Parascaniornis is now considered a junior synonym of Baptornis, while Gallornis may be an early member of the group Galloanserae.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, más tarde se consideró al primero como un sinónimo más moderno de Baptornis (un ave hesperornitina), mientras que el último puede ser un miembro primitivo del grupo Galloanserae.

facts.statement: The Paleobiology Database lists the parent group of Torotix as Pelecaniformes.
Torotix lived during the Maastrichtian stage, from 72.2 to 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Maastrichtian to Maastrichtian (72.2 to 66 million years ago)
